editorial:
Imagine being a college freshman who is already a total disaster. That is exactly where you find Brian Kieslowski. Instead of a sweet rom-com, you get a funny and stressful ride as Brian tries to navigate his first real relationship. Things go south fast when he finds out he got his girlfriend pregnant with twins. To make it even crazier, the girl is suddenly diving deep into a strict religious phase. You will feel for Brian as he bumbles through every single conversation, trying to be a good guy while the world collapses around him. The vibe is lighthearted but it asks some real questions about what it actually means to do the right thing when you are totally unqualified for the job.

What really works here is the awkward chemistry between the leads. The pacing is quick, and the jokes land because the situations feel so relatable if you have ever felt out of your depth. While some of the plot twists feel a bit sudden, the humor carries it through. If you are in the mood for a quirky indie flick, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want to keep it in your physical collection for the best picture quality. It is a great pick for a lazy Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Brian stops trying to be the perfect person everyone expects and starts being honest about his fears. He and the girl realize that their new beliefs and the stress of the twins are pushing them apart. They decide to handle the pregnancy as a team, but not necessarily as a romantic couple. The movie wraps up with them finding a middle ground, showing that growing up often means making messy compromises.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cringe comedy and stories about young adults figuring out life.
